- Checksum.sumMod256(byte[] data) sums every supplied byte as unsigned and returns the sum modulo 256. TextEncoder.encodePayload(String text) UTF-8 encodes text, prepends a two-byte unsigned big-endian payload length, and appends exactly one checksum byte computed over ONLY the two length bytes plus UTF-8 payload bytes, never over the checksum slot itself. Both encodePayload and decodePayload must literally obtain that checksum input with `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1)` and compare the expected checksum to `(frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF)`. Calling Checksum.sumMod256(frame) on the complete frame during validation is forbidden because it incorrectly includes the checksum byte
- TextEncoder.decodePayload(byte[] frame) requires the frame length to be exactly 2+L+1, validates the prefix-only checksum before strict UTF-8 decoding, and `TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界"))` must round-trip directly even without a matrix
- TextEncoder.bytesToBits(byte[] bytes) emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal assignment `bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;`. TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits) MUST accept every non-null bit-array length, including zero and lengths not divisible by eight, and pads the final partial byte with trailing zero bits. It must literally allocate `byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8];` and set each true bit with `result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));`. A check, exception, assertion, early return, or truncation based on `bits.length % 8 != 0` is forbidden
- the direct padding fixture is literal: `TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(new boolean[]{true,false,false,false,false,false,false,false,true})` returns a two-byte array whose unsigned values are 128 and 128; MainTest must include this fixture so rejecting or dropping the ninth bit cannot pass
- FinderPattern.reservedMask(size), FinderPattern.place(matrix), FinderPattern.verify(matrix), and ZigZag.traversal(size,reserved) use one identical three-finder reserved-cell definition. QRCodec.encode writes framed payload bits to the traversal prefix and leaves every unused data cell false
- ZigZag.traversal uses one exact finite two-pass row-serpentine algorithm, not an open-ended diagonal state machine: first validate that reserved is exactly size by size, set `int count = 0;`, scan every row and column once and increment count only for `!reserved[row][col]`, then allocate exactly `int[][] result = new int[count][2];`. In a second bounded `for (int row = 0; row < size; row++)` pass, visit columns 0 through size-1 on even rows and size-1 through 0 on odd rows, append `[row,col]` only when the cell is not reserved, and return after exactly count insertions
- ZigZag.traversal MUST NOT allocate `new int[size * size][2]`, MUST NOT terminate on `index < size * size`, and MUST NOT use any while loop or leave zero-coordinate placeholder entries. These forms can never terminate after reserved cells are skipped and previously caused Index 21 out-of-bounds. Both encode and decode use the exact returned `count` coordinates without re-filtering them
- MatrixValidator accepts only odd sizes at least 21. MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) derives capacity by counting false entries in FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and may round that count down to a multiple of eight; it must not subtract three pattern areas in a way that double-counts overlaps. QRDetector.readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix) deliberately returns every unreserved traversal bit, whose length need not be divisible by eight; no caller may assume its length is byte-aligned
- QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes first calls readDataBits, then calls TextEncoder.bitsToBytes on that complete possibly-non-byte-aligned array. It reads unsigned L from the first two resulting bytes, computes exactly `int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;`, rejects insufficient bytes, then literally uses `byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);`, validates that exact frame with TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame), and returns frame. It ignores only the zero-filled unused matrix suffix by truncating according to L; it must never pass all capacity bytes to an exact-length decoder
- QRCodec.encode(String,int), encode(String), and decode(QRMatrix) use that single framing path. Auto-size must literally begin with `int size = 21;`, then add two while capacity is insufficient; QRCodec must never read a MatrixValidator.MIN_SIZE field or any other visibility-sensitive constant. QRRenderer.render produces exactly one deterministic line per matrix row and performs no I/O
- Because every project class is in Java's unnamed/default package, MainTest imports ONLY `org.junit.jupiter.api.Test` and static members from `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`. It directly refers to QRCodec, QRMatrix, TextEncoder, QRRenderer, and Main without importing them. Lines such as `import QRCodec;`, `import QRMatrix;`, or imports of any other default-package project class are invalid Java and strictly forbidden
- Main.main encodes, renders, and decodes one fixed short string, prints at most one concise result, and returns normally. MainTest contains exactly three concise JUnit Jupiter tests: (1) Main.main returns normally; (2) the exact nine-bit padding fixture above, direct `TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界"))`, plus `codec.decode(codec.encode("hello-世界"))` all round-trip and rendering has one line per row; (3) corrupting a copied finder cell `[0][0]` makes decode throw IllegalArgumentException. This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):

- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java deterministic QR-like codec and padding contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/QRMatrix.java, src/main/java/Checksum.java, src/main/java/ZigZag.java, src/main/java/FinderPattern.java, src/main/java/TextEncoder.java, src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java, src/main/java/QRDetector.java, src/main/java/QRCodec.java, src/main/java/QRRenderer.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; every class is in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Maven Surefire plugin; no runtime dependency, network, GUI, input, randomness, clock, filesystem image, or third-party QR library is allowed
- Checksum.sumMod256(byte[] data) sums every supplied byte as unsigned and returns the sum modulo 256. TextEncoder.encodePayload(String text) UTF-8 encodes text, prepends a two-byte unsigned big-endian payload length, and appends exactly one checksum byte computed over ONLY the two length bytes plus UTF-8 payload bytes, never over the checksum slot itself. Both encodePayload and decodePayload must literally obtain that checksum input with `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1)` and compare the expected checksum to `(frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF)`. Calling Checksum.sumMod256(frame) on the complete frame during validation is forbidden because it incorrectly includes the checksum byte
- TextEncoder.decodePayload(byte[] frame) requires the frame length to be exactly 2+L+1, validates the prefix-only checksum before strict UTF-8 decoding, and `TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界"))` must round-trip directly even without a matrix
- TextEncoder.bytesToBits(byte[] bytes) emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal assignment `bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;`. TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits) MUST accept every non-null bit-array length, including zero and lengths not divisible by eight, and pads the final partial byte with trailing zero bits. It must literally allocate `byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8];` and set each true bit with `result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));`. A check, exception, assertion, early return, or truncation based on `bits.length % 8 != 0` is forbidden

In a second bounded `for (int row = 0; row < size; row++)` pass, visit columns 0 through size-1 on even rows and size-1 through 0 on odd rows, append `[row,col]` only when the cell is not reserved, and return after exactly count insertions

It directly refers to QRCodec, QRMatrix, TextEncoder, QRRenderer, and Main without importing them. src/main/java/QRMatrix.java: class QRMatrix { public QRMatrix(int size); public int getSize(); public boolean get(int row, int col); public void set(int row, int col, boolean val); public boolean[][] copyCells(); }. Semantics: size immutable, cells are square size x size. Bounds checks throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. copyCells returns a deep copy. No IO.

src/main/java/Checksum.java: class Checksum { public static int sumMod256(byte[] data); }. Semantics: sums every provided byte as unsigned (b & 0xFF), returns sum % 256. No side effects.

src/main/java/ZigZag.java: class ZigZag { public static int[][] traversal(int size, boolean[][] reserved); }. Semantics: validates reserved is size x size. Two-pass bounded row-serpentine algorithm: First pass counts only unreserved cells with int count = 0; then literally allocates int[][] result = new int[count][2];. Second pass: for (int row = 0; row < size; row++) { if (row % 2 == 0) iterate col 0..size-1; else iterate col size-1..0; append coordinates only when !reserved[row][col]; }. No while loops, MUST NOT allocate new int[size * size][2], MUST NOT use index < size * size termination, and MUST NOT emit placeholder zeros. Consumers (encode/decode) use returned coordinates directly without re-filtering.

src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: class FinderPattern { public static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size); public static void place(QRMatrix matrix); public static void verify(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: Defines and enforces exactly three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left. reservedMask marks those cells true; throws IllegalArgumentException if size is even or < 21. place sets those cells to true in the given matrix. verify ensures those cells are true and reserved pattern matches exactly; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.

src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: class TextEncoder { public static byte[] encodePayload(String text); public static String decodePayload(byte[] frame); public static boolean[] bytesToBits(byte[] bytes); public static byte[] bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits); }. Semantics:
- encodePayload: UTF-8 encodes text; builds frame [lenHi, lenLo, payload..., checksum]; computes checksum ONLY over the prefix (two length bytes plus payload) via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; writes checksum as final byte; never computes over the complete frame.
- decodePayload: requires frame length == 2 + L + 1; validates checksum using the same prefix-only java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and compares to (frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF); decodes payload as strict UTF-8 and returns String. Throws IllegalArgumentException on length mismatch or checksum mismatch, and CharacterCodingException-derived errors are wrapped or rethrown as IllegalArgumentException.
- bytesToBits: emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal statement bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;.
- bitsToBytes: accepts any non-null bit array length (including 0 and non-multiples of 8). It must literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set each true bit with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));. No modulo-length rejection, exceptions, assertions, early returns, or truncation if bits.length % 8 != 0.

src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: class MatrixValidator { public static void ensureValidSize(int size); public static int capacityBits(int size); }. Semantics: ensureValidSize accepts odd sizes >= 21, else throws IllegalArgumentException. capacityBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and counts false entries; may round down to multiple of 8; must not double-count or subtract heuristically.

src/main/java/QRDetector.java: class QRDetector { public static boolean[] readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix); public static byte[] extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: readDataBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask and ZigZag.traversal to read all unreserved cells in order; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes converts all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than two bytes available, throws IllegalArgumentException; reads unsigned length L from first two bytes; computes exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; rejects insufficient bytes; literally truncates via byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); returns frame. It ignores only zero-padded unused suffix dictated by L and never passes all capacity bytes to decodePayload.

src/main/java/QRCodec.java: class QRCodec { public QRMatrix encode(String text); public QRMatrix encode(String text, int size); public String decode(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: encode(String,int) validates size via MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; computes reserved mask and traversal; encodes frame via TextEncoder.encodePayload; writes TextEncoder.bytesToBits into traversal order; leaves all extra unfilled cells false; calls FinderPattern.place; returns populated matrix. encode(String) auto-sizes literally starting with int size = 21; increments by 2 until MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) >= frameBitLength; delegates to encode(String,int). decode verifies finders via FinderPattern.verify, extracts frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes, and returns TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).

src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: class QRRenderer { public static String render(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: returns a deterministic textual representation with exactly one line per matrix row; no IO side-effects.

src/main/java/Main.java: class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }. Semantics: Demonstrates encode->render->decode pipeline on a fixed short string like "hello-世界"; prints at most one concise line; returns normally.

src/test/java/MainTest.java: JUnit 5 tests in default package; imports only org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*. Exactly three tests: (1) Main.main does not throw; (2) literal nine-bit fixture new boolean[]{true,false,false,false,false,false,false,false,true} maps via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes to two bytes whose unsigned values are 128 and 128; TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRCodec.decode(QRCodec.encode("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRRenderer.render emits exactly one line per matrix row; (3) flipping a copied finder cell [0][0] causes IllegalArgumentException during decode.

src/main/java/QRMatrix.java: class QRMatrix { public QRMatrix(int size); public int getSize(); public boolean get(int row, int col); public void set(int row, int col, boolean val); public boolean[][] copyCells(); }. Semantics: size immutable, cells are square size x size. Bounds checks throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. copyCells returns a deep copy. No IO.

src/main/java/Checksum.java: class Checksum { public static int sumMod256(byte[] data); }. Semantics: sums every provided byte as unsigned (b & 0xFF), returns sum % 256. No side effects.

src/main/java/ZigZag.java: class ZigZag { public static int[][] traversal(int size, boolean[][] reserved); }. Semantics: validates reserved is size x size. Two-pass bounded row-serpentine algorithm: First pass counts only unreserved cells with int count = 0; then literally allocates int[][] result = new int[count][2];. Second pass: for (int row = 0; row < size; row++) { if (row % 2 == 0) iterate col 0..size-1; else iterate col size-1..0; append coordinates only when !reserved[row][col]; }. No while loops, MUST NOT allocate new int[size * size][2], MUST NOT use index < size * size termination, and MUST NOT emit placeholder zeros. Consumers (encode/decode) use returned coordinates directly without re-filtering.

src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: class FinderPattern { public static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size); public static void place(QRMatrix matrix); public static void verify(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: Defines and enforces exactly three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left. reservedMask marks those cells true; throws IllegalArgumentException if size is even or < 21. place sets those cells to true in the given matrix. verify ensures those cells are true and reserved pattern matches exactly; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.

src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: class TextEncoder { public static byte[] encodePayload(String text); public static String decodePayload(byte[] frame); public static boolean[] bytesToBits(byte[] bytes); public static byte[] bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits); }. Semantics:
- encodePayload: UTF-8 encodes text; builds frame [lenHi, lenLo, payload..., checksum]; computes checksum ONLY over the prefix (two length bytes plus payload) via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; writes checksum as final byte; never computes over the complete frame.
- decodePayload: requires frame length == 2 + L + 1; validates checksum using the same prefix-only java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and compares to (frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF); decodes payload as strict UTF-8 and returns String. Throws IllegalArgumentException on length mismatch or checksum mismatch, and CharacterCodingException-derived errors are wrapped or rethrown as IllegalArgumentException.
- bytesToBits: emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal statement bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;.
- bitsToBytes: accepts any non-null bit array length (including 0 and non-multiples of 8). It must literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set each true bit with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));. No modulo-length rejection, exceptions, assertions, early returns, or truncation if bits.length % 8 != 0.

src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: class MatrixValidator { public static void ensureValidSize(int size); public static int capacityBits(int size); }. Semantics: ensureValidSize accepts odd sizes >= 21, else throws IllegalArgumentException. capacityBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and counts false entries; may round down to multiple of 8; must not double-count or subtract heuristically.

src/main/java/QRDetector.java: class QRDetector { public static boolean[] readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix); public static byte[] extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: readDataBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask and ZigZag.traversal to read all unreserved cells in order; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes converts all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than two bytes available, throws IllegalArgumentException; reads unsigned length L from first two bytes; computes exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; rejects insufficient bytes; literally truncates via byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); returns frame. It ignores only zero-padded unused suffix dictated by L and never passes all capacity bytes to decodePayload.

src/main/java/QRCodec.java: class QRCodec { public QRMatrix encode(String text); public QRMatrix encode(String text, int size); public String decode(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: encode(String,int) validates size via MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; computes reserved mask and traversal; encodes frame via TextEncoder.encodePayload; writes TextEncoder.bytesToBits into traversal order; leaves all extra unfilled cells false; calls FinderPattern.place; returns populated matrix. encode(String) auto-sizes literally starting with int size = 21; increments by 2 until MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) >= frameBitLength; delegates to encode(String,int). decode verifies finders via FinderPattern.verify, extracts frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes, and returns TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).

src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: class QRRenderer { public static String render(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: returns a deterministic textual representation with exactly one line per matrix row; no IO side-effects.

src/main/java/Main.java: class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }. Semantics: Demonstrates encode->render->decode pipeline on a fixed short string like "hello-世界"; prints at most one concise line; returns normally.

src/test/java/MainTest.java: JUnit 5 tests in default package; imports only org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*. Exactly three tests: (1) Main.main does not throw; (2) literal nine-bit fixture new boolean[]{true,false,false,false,false,false,false,false,true} maps via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes to two bytes whose unsigned values are 128 and 128; TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRCodec.decode(QRCodec.encode("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRRenderer.render emits exactly one line per matrix row; (3) flipping a copied finder cell [0][0] causes IllegalArgumentException during decode.

Allowed import/include directions: Higher-level classes depend on already-declared lower-level modules: QRCodec depends on TextEncoder, MatrixValidator, ZigZag, FinderPattern, and QRMatrix; QRDetector depends on TextEncoder, ZigZag, FinderPattern; QRRenderer depends on QRMatrix; Main depends on QRCodec and QRRenderer. No circular dependencies. All classes reside in the default package (unnamed), and tests must not import these classes explicitly.","Shared Knowledge":"Repository targets a Java 11 Maven project. src/main/java/QRMatrix.java: class QRMatrix { public QRMatrix(int size); public int getSize(); public boolean get(int row, int col); public void set(int row, int col, boolean val); public boolean[][] copyCells(); }. Semantics: size immutable, cells are square size x size. Bounds checks throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. copyCells returns a deep copy. No IO.

src/main/java/Checksum.java: class Checksum { public static int sumMod256(byte[] data); }. Semantics: sums every provided byte as unsigned (b & 0xFF), returns sum % 256. No side effects.

src/main/java/ZigZag.java: class ZigZag { public static int[][] traversal(int size, boolean[][] reserved); }. Semantics: validates reserved is size x size. Two-pass bounded row-serpentine algorithm: First pass counts only unreserved cells with int count = 0; then literally allocates int[][] result = new int[count][2];. Second pass: for (int row = 0; row < size; row++) { if (row % 2 == 0) iterate col 0..size-1; else iterate col size-1..0; append coordinates only when !reserved[row][col]; }. No while loops, MUST NOT allocate new int[size * size][2], MUST NOT use index < size * size termination, and MUST NOT emit placeholder zeros. Consumers (encode/decode) use returned coordinates directly without re-filtering.

src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: class FinderPattern { public static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size); public static void place(QRMatrix matrix); public static void verify(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: Defines and enforces exactly three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left. reservedMask marks those cells true; throws IllegalArgumentException if size is even or < 21. place sets those cells to true in the given matrix. verify ensures those cells are true and reserved pattern matches exactly; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.

src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: class TextEncoder { public static byte[] encodePayload(String text); public static String decodePayload(byte[] frame); public static boolean[] bytesToBits(byte[] bytes); public static byte[] bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits); }. Semantics:
- encodePayload: UTF-8 encodes text; builds frame [lenHi, lenLo, payload..., checksum]; computes checksum ONLY over the prefix (two length bytes plus payload) via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; writes checksum as final byte; never computes over the complete frame.
- decodePayload: requires frame length == 2 + L + 1; validates checksum using the same prefix-only java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and compares to (frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF); decodes payload as strict UTF-8 and returns String. Throws IllegalArgumentException on length mismatch or checksum mismatch, and CharacterCodingException-derived errors are wrapped or rethrown as IllegalArgumentException.
- bytesToBits: emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal statement bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;.
- bitsToBytes: accepts any non-null bit array length (including 0 and non-multiples of 8). It must literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set each true bit with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));. No modulo-length rejection, exceptions, assertions, early returns, or truncation if bits.length % 8 != 0.

src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: class MatrixValidator { public static void ensureValidSize(int size); public static int capacityBits(int size); }. Semantics: ensureValidSize accepts odd sizes >= 21, else throws IllegalArgumentException. capacityBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and counts false entries; may round down to multiple of 8; must not double-count or subtract heuristically.

src/main/java/QRDetector.java: class QRDetector { public static boolean[] readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix); public static byte[] extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: readDataBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask and ZigZag.traversal to read all unreserved cells in order; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes converts all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than two bytes available, throws IllegalArgumentException; reads unsigned length L from first two bytes; computes exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; rejects insufficient bytes; literally truncates via byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); returns frame. It ignores only zero-padded unused suffix dictated by L and never passes all capacity bytes to decodePayload.

src/main/java/QRCodec.java: class QRCodec { public QRMatrix encode(String text); public QRMatrix encode(String text, int size); public String decode(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: encode(String,int) validates size via MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; computes reserved mask and traversal; encodes frame via TextEncoder.encodePayload; writes TextEncoder.bytesToBits into traversal order; leaves all extra unfilled cells false; calls FinderPattern.place; returns populated matrix. encode(String) auto-sizes literally starting with int size = 21; increments by 2 until MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) >= frameBitLength; delegates to encode(String,int). decode verifies finders via FinderPattern.verify, extracts frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes, and returns TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).

src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: class QRRenderer { public static String render(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: returns a deterministic textual representation with exactly one line per matrix row; no IO side-effects.

src/main/java/Main.java: class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }. Semantics: Demonstrates encode->render->decode pipeline on a fixed short string like "hello-世界"; prints at most one concise line; returns normally.

src/test/java/MainTest.java: JUnit 5 tests in default package; imports only org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*. Exactly three tests: (1) Main.main does not throw; (2) literal nine-bit fixture new boolean[]{true,false,false,false,false,false,false,false,true} maps via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes to two bytes whose unsigned values are 128 and 128; TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRCodec.decode(QRCodec.encode("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRRenderer.render emits exactly one line per matrix row; (3) flipping a copied finder cell [0][0] causes IllegalArgumentException during decode.

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: QR Code Gen.&Det..

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java deterministic QR-like codec and padding contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/QRMatrix.java, src/main/java/Checksum.java, src/main/java/ZigZag.java, src/main/java/FinderPattern.java, src/main/java/TextEncoder.java, src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java, src/main/java/QRDetector.java, src/main/java/QRCodec.java, src/main/java/QRRenderer.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; every class is in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Maven Surefire plugin; no runtime dependency, network, GUI, input, randomness, clock, filesystem image, or third-party QR library is allowed
- Checksum.sumMod256(byte[] data) sums every supplied byte as unsigned and returns the sum modulo 256. TextEncoder.encodePayload(String text) UTF-8 encodes text, prepends a two-byte unsigned big-endian payload length, and appends exactly one checksum byte computed over ONLY the two length bytes plus UTF-8 payload bytes, never over the checksum slot itself. Both encodePayload and decodePayload must literally obtain that checksum input with `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1)` and compare the expected checksum to `(frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF)`. Calling Checksum.sumMod256(frame) on the complete frame during validation is forbidden because it incorrectly includes the checksum byte
- TextEncoder.decodePayload(byte[] frame) requires the frame length to be exactly 2+L+1, validates the prefix-only checksum before strict UTF-8 decoding, and `TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界"))` must round-trip directly even without a matrix
- TextEncoder.bytesToBits(byte[] bytes) emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal assignment `bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;`. TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits) MUST accept every non-null bit-array length, including zero and lengths not divisible by eight, and pads the final partial byte with trailing zero bits. It must literally allocate `byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8];` and set each true bit with `result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));`. A check, exception, assertion, early return, or truncation based on `bits.length % 8 != 0` is forbidden
- the direct padding fixture is literal: `TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(new boolean[]{true,false,false,false,false,false,false,false,true})` returns a two-byte array whose unsigned values are 128 and 128; MainTest must include this fixture so rejecting or dropping the ninth bit cannot pass
- FinderPattern.reservedMask(size), FinderPattern.place(matrix), FinderPattern.verify(matrix), and ZigZag.traversal(size,reserved) use one identical three-finder reserved-cell definition. QRCodec.encode writes framed payload bits to the traversal prefix and leaves every unused data cell false
- ZigZag.traversal uses one exact finite two-pass row-serpentine algorithm, not an open-ended diagonal state machine: first validate that reserved is exactly size by size, set `int count = 0;`, scan every row and column once and increment count only for `!reserved[row][col]`, then allocate exactly `int[][] result = new int[count][2];`. In a second bounded `for (int row = 0; row < size; row++)` pass, visit columns 0 through size-1 on even rows and size-1 through 0 on odd rows, append `[row,col]` only when the cell is not reserved, and return after exactly count insertions
- ZigZag.traversal MUST NOT allocate `new int[size * size][2]`, MUST NOT terminate on `index < size * size`, and MUST NOT use any while loop or leave zero-coordinate placeholder entries. These forms can never terminate after reserved cells are skipped and previously caused Index 21 out-of-bounds. Both encode and decode use the exact returned `count` coordinates without re-filtering them
- MatrixValidator accepts only odd sizes at least 21. MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) derives capacity by counting false entries in FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and may round that count down to a multiple of eight; it must not subtract three pattern areas in a way that double-counts overlaps. QRDetector.readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix) deliberately returns every unreserved traversal bit, whose length need not be divisible by eight; no caller may assume its length is byte-aligned
- QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes first calls readDataBits, then calls TextEncoder.bitsToBytes on that complete possibly-non-byte-aligned array. It reads unsigned L from the first two resulting bytes, computes exactly `int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;`, rejects insufficient bytes, then literally uses `byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);`, validates that exact frame with TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame), and returns frame. It ignores only the zero-filled unused matrix suffix by truncating according to L; it must never pass all capacity bytes to an exact-length decoder
- QRCodec.encode(String,int), encode(String), and decode(QRMatrix) use that single framing path. Auto-size must literally begin with `int size = 21;`, then add two while capacity is insufficient; QRCodec must never read a MatrixValidator.MIN_SIZE field or any other visibility-sensitive constant. QRRenderer.render produces exactly one deterministic line per matrix row and performs no I/O
- Because every project class is in Java's unnamed/default package, MainTest imports ONLY `org.junit.jupiter.api.Test` and static members from `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`. Second pass: for (int row = 0; row < size; row++) { if (row % 2 == 0) iterate col 0..size-1; else iterate col size-1..0; append coordinates only when !reserved[row][col]; }. No while loops, MUST NOT allocate new int[size * size][2], MUST NOT use index < size * size termination, and MUST NOT emit placeholder zeros. Consumers (encode/decode) use returned coordinates directly without re-filtering.

src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: class FinderPattern { public static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size); public static void place(QRMatrix matrix); public static void verify(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: Defines and enforces exactly three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left. reservedMask marks those cells true; throws IllegalArgumentException if size is even or < 21. place sets those cells to true in the given matrix. verify ensures those cells are true and reserved pattern matches exactly; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.

src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: class TextEncoder { public static byte[] encodePayload(String text); public static String decodePayload(byte[] frame); public static boolean[] bytesToBits(byte[] bytes); public static byte[] bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits); }. Semantics:
- encodePayload: UTF-8 encodes text; builds frame [lenHi, lenLo, payload..., checksum]; computes checksum ONLY over the prefix (two length bytes plus payload) via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; writes checksum as final byte; never computes over the complete frame.
- decodePayload: requires frame length == 2 + L + 1; validates checksum using the same prefix-only java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and compares to (frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF); decodes payload as strict UTF-8 and returns String. Throws IllegalArgumentException on length mismatch or checksum mismatch, and CharacterCodingException-derived errors are wrapped or rethrown as IllegalArgumentException.
- bytesToBits: emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal statement bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;.
- bitsToBytes: accepts any non-null bit array length (including 0 and non-multiples of 8). It must literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set each true bit with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));. No modulo-length rejection, exceptions, assertions, early returns, or truncation if bits.length % 8 != 0.

src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: class MatrixValidator { public static void ensureValidSize(int size); public static int capacityBits(int size); }. Semantics: ensureValidSize accepts odd sizes >= 21, else throws IllegalArgumentException. capacityBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and counts false entries; may round down to multiple of 8; must not double-count or subtract heuristically.

src/main/java/QRDetector.java: class QRDetector { public static boolean[] readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix); public static byte[] extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: readDataBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask and ZigZag.traversal to read all unreserved cells in order; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes converts all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than two bytes available, throws IllegalArgumentException; reads unsigned length L from first two bytes; computes exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; rejects insufficient bytes; literally truncates via byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); returns frame. It ignores only zero-padded unused suffix dictated by L and never passes all capacity bytes to decodePayload.

src/main/java/QRCodec.java: class QRCodec { public QRMatrix encode(String text); public QRMatrix encode(String text, int size); public String decode(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: encode(String,int) validates size via MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; computes reserved mask and traversal; encodes frame via TextEncoder.encodePayload; writes TextEncoder.bytesToBits into traversal order; leaves all extra unfilled cells false; calls FinderPattern.place; returns populated matrix. encode(String) auto-sizes literally starting with int size = 21; increments by 2 until MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) >= frameBitLength; delegates to encode(String,int). decode verifies finders via FinderPattern.verify, extracts frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes, and returns TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).

src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: class QRRenderer { public static String render(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: returns a deterministic textual representation with exactly one line per matrix row; no IO side-effects.

src/main/java/Main.java: class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }. Semantics: Demonstrates encode->render->decode pipeline on a fixed short string like "hello-世界"; prints at most one concise line; returns normally.

Project-specific Java deterministic QR-like codec and padding contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/QRMatrix.java, src/main/java/Checksum.java, src/main/java/ZigZag.java, src/main/java/FinderPattern.java, src/main/java/TextEncoder.java, src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java, src/main/java/QRDetector.java, src/main/java/QRCodec.java, src/main/java/QRRenderer.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; every class is in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Maven Surefire plugin; no runtime dependency, network, GUI, input, randomness, clock, filesystem image, or third-party QR library is allowed
- Checksum.sumMod256(byte[] data) sums every supplied byte as unsigned and returns the sum modulo 256. TextEncoder.encodePayload(String text) UTF-8 encodes text, prepends a two-byte unsigned big-endian payload length, and appends exactly one checksum byte computed over ONLY the two length bytes plus UTF-8 payload bytes, never over the checksum slot itself. Both encodePayload and decodePayload must literally obtain that checksum input with `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1)` and compare the expected checksum to `(frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF)`. Calling Checksum.sumMod256(frame) on the complete frame during validation is forbidden because it incorrectly includes the checksum byte
- TextEncoder.decodePayload(byte[] frame) requires the frame length to be exactly 2+L+1, validates the prefix-only checksum before strict UTF-8 decoding, and `TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界"))` must round-trip directly even without a matrix
- TextEncoder.bytesToBits(byte[] bytes) emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal assignment `bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;`. TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits) MUST accept every non-null bit-array length, including zero and lengths not divisible by eight, and pads the final partial byte with trailing zero bits. It must literally allocate `byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8];` and set each true bit with `result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));`. A check, exception, assertion, early return, or truncation based on `bits.length % 8 != 0` is forbidden
- the direct padding fixture is literal: `TextEncoder.bitsToBytes(new boolean[]{true,false,false,false,false,false,false,false,true})` returns a two-byte array whose unsigned values are 128 and 128; MainTest must include this fixture so rejecting or dropping the ninth bit cannot pass
- FinderPattern.reservedMask(size), FinderPattern.place(matrix), FinderPattern.verify(matrix), and ZigZag.traversal(size,reserved) use one identical three-finder reserved-cell definition. QRCodec.encode writes framed payload bits to the traversal prefix and leaves every unused data cell false
- ZigZag.traversal uses one exact finite two-pass row-serpentine algorithm, not an open-ended diagonal state machine: first validate that reserved is exactly size by size, set `int count = 0;`, scan every row and column once and increment count only for `!reserved[row][col]`, then allocate exactly `int[][] result = new int[count][2];`. In a second bounded `for (int row = 0; row < size; row++)` pass, visit columns 0 through size-1 on even rows and size-1 through 0 on odd rows, append `[row,col]` only when the cell is not reserved, and return after exactly count insertions
- ZigZag.traversal MUST NOT allocate `new int[size * size][2]`, MUST NOT terminate on `index < size * size`, and MUST NOT use any while loop or leave zero-coordinate placeholder entries. These forms can never terminate after reserved cells are skipped and previously caused Index 21 out-of-bounds. Both encode and decode use the exact returned `count` coordinates without re-filtering them
- MatrixValidator accepts only odd sizes at least 21. MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) derives capacity by counting false entries in FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and may round that count down to a multiple of eight; it must not subtract three pattern areas in a way that double-counts overlaps. QRDetector.readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix) deliberately returns every unreserved traversal bit, whose length need not be divisible by eight; no caller may assume its length is byte-aligned
- QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes first calls readDataBits, then calls TextEncoder.bitsToBytes on that complete possibly-non-byte-aligned array. It reads unsigned L from the first two resulting bytes, computes exactly `int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;`, rejects insufficient bytes, then literally uses `byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);`, validates that exact frame with TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame), and returns frame. It ignores only the zero-filled unused matrix suffix by truncating according to L; it must never pass all capacity bytes to an exact-length decoder
- QRCodec.encode(String,int), encode(String), and decode(QRMatrix) use that single framing path. Auto-size must literally begin with `int size = 21;`, then add two while capacity is insufficient; QRCodec must never read a MatrixValidator.MIN_SIZE field or any other visibility-sensitive constant. QRRenderer.render produces exactly one deterministic line per matrix row and performs no I/O
- Because every project class is in Java's unnamed/default package, MainTest imports ONLY `org.junit.jupiter.api.Test` and static members from `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`. It directly refers to QRCodec, QRMatrix, TextEncoder, QRRenderer, and Main without importing them. Lines such as `import QRCodec;`, `import QRMatrix;`, or imports of any other default-package project class are invalid Java and strictly forbidden
- Main.main encodes, renders, and decodes one fixed short string, prints at most one concise result, and returns normally. MainTest contains exactly three concise JUnit Jupiter tests: (1) Main.main returns normally; (2) the exact nine-bit padding fixture above, direct `TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界"))`, plus `codec.decode(codec.encode("hello-世界"))` all round-trip and rendering has one line per row; (3) corrupting a copied finder cell `[0][0]` makes decode throw IllegalArgumentException. Tests never locate an arbitrary payload bit or assume unused traversal length is divisible by eight

The runtime entry Main is thin and side-effect-free beyond a small fixed demonstration. All core logic is pure and testable, with no GUI or runtime dependencies. The single JUnit 5 test file validates padding, framing, traversal, finder verification, capacity rules, and corruption rejection. We strictly comply with the FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE QR JAVA PADDING CHECKLIST: prefix-only checksum using java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1); TextEncoder.bytesToBits uses the literal MSB-first emission line bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;; TextEncoder.bitsToBytes accepts any bit length and literally allocates byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and sets bits with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));; ZigZag.traversal performs a two-pass bounded serpentine with exact int[][] result = new int[count][2]; and no while loops; QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes reads all unreserved bits, converts all with the padding implementation, obtains L from first two bytes, computes int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;, truncates with byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);, validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame), and returns frame. FinderPattern.reservedMask/place/verify use a single consistent three-finder definition; QRCodec auto-size literally begins with int size = 21; and increments by 2 until capacity fits. Rendering emits exactly one line per matrix row.

Per-file tasks and contracts ordered by dependency:
1) pom.xml: Java 11 toolchain; depend on org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter in test scope; configure Maven Surefire to run JUnit 5; no runtime deps.
2) src/main/java/QRMatrix.java: Immutable size; boolean[][] cells; construction validating square; getters/setters; copy(); matrix-level helpers used by renderer and validators. No IO.
3) src/main/java/Checksum.java: static int sumMod256(byte[] data): sum bytes as unsigned, return sum % 256. No other functions.
4) src/main/java/ZigZag.java: static int[][] traversal(int size, boolean[][] reserved): two-pass bounded algorithm. First pass counts only unreserved cells and literally allocates int[][] result = new int[count][2];. Second pass iterates rows 0..size-1, columns ascend on even rows and descend on odd rows, appends coordinates only when not reserved. No while loops. No new int[size * size][2].
5) src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size): marks three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, bottom-left; throws if size < 21 or even. static void place(QRMatrix): sets those finder cells true. static void verify(QRMatrix): ensures those exact cells are true and others in reserved mask remain reserved; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.
6) src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: encodePayload(String text): UTF-8 encode; build frame [lenHi,lenLo,payload,checksum]; checksum computed ONLY over prefix via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; never over the complete frame. decodePayload(byte[] frame): verify frame length equals 2+L+1; validate prefix-only checksum with the same Arrays.copyOf; return strict UTF-8 string. bytesToBits(byte[] bytes): exact MSB-first emission with bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;; bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits): accept any length; literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set bits via result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));; no modulo-length rejection or truncation.
7) src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: static void ensureValidSize(int size): only odd sizes >= 21. static int capacityBits(int size): count unreserved cells (false entries) from FinderPattern.reservedMask(size); may round down to multiple of 8; does not double-count or heuristically subtract.
8) src/main/java/QRDetector.java: readDataBits(QRMatrix): use reservedMask and ZigZag traversal to read every unreserved cell; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix): convert all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than 2 bytes, throw; compute length from first two bytes as unsigned; compute exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; reject insufficient bytes; literally byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validate by TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); return frame.
9) src/main/java/QRCodec.java: encode(String text, int size): MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; compute reserved mask; capacityBits; TextEncoder.encodePayload; write bytesToBits into traversal order, leaving any extra cells false; FinderPattern.place; return matrix. encode(String text): auto-size literally starting with int size = 21; while capacity < frameBitsLen, size += 2; then encode(String,int). decode(QRMatrix): FinderPattern.verify; get frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes; return TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).
10) src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: render(QRMatrix): deterministic string, exactly one line per row, no IO side-effects; e.g., '#' for true and '.' for false.
11) src/main/java/Main.java: small demo: String msg = "hello-世界"; encode; render; decode; print concise result; return normally.
12) src/test/java/MainTest.java: single JUnit 5 file with exactly three tests: (1) Main.main returns normally; (2) bitsToBytes 9-bit fixture yields unsigned 128,128; direct TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRCodec.decode(QRCodec.encode("hello-世界")) round-trips; rendering has one line per matrix row; (3) corrupting a copied finder cell [0][0] causes decode to throw IllegalArgumentException.

src/main/java/QRMatrix.java: class QRMatrix { public QRMatrix(int size); public int getSize(); public boolean get(int row, int col); public void set(int row, int col, boolean val); public boolean[][] copyCells(); }. Semantics: size immutable, cells are square size x size. Bounds checks throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. copyCells returns a deep copy. No IO.

src/main/java/Checksum.java: class Checksum { public static int sumMod256(byte[] data); }. Semantics: sums every provided byte as unsigned (b & 0xFF), returns sum % 256. No side effects.

src/main/java/ZigZag.java: class ZigZag { public static int[][] traversal(int size, boolean[][] reserved); }. Semantics: validates reserved is size x size. Two-pass bounded row-serpentine algorithm: First pass counts only unreserved cells with int count = 0; then literally allocates int[][] result = new int[count][2];. Second pass: for (int row = 0; row < size; row++) { if (row % 2 == 0) iterate col 0..size-1; else iterate col size-1..0; append coordinates only when !reserved[row][col]; }. No while loops, MUST NOT allocate new int[size * size][2], MUST NOT use index < size * size termination, and MUST NOT emit placeholder zeros. Consumers (encode/decode) use returned coordinates directly without re-filtering.

src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: class FinderPattern { public static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size); public static void place(QRMatrix matrix); public static void verify(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: Defines and enforces exactly three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left. reservedMask marks those cells true; throws IllegalArgumentException if size is even or < 21. place sets those cells to true in the given matrix. verify ensures those cells are true and reserved pattern matches exactly; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.

src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: class TextEncoder { public static byte[] encodePayload(String text); public static String decodePayload(byte[] frame); public static boolean[] bytesToBits(byte[] bytes); public static byte[] bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits); }. Semantics:
- encodePayload: UTF-8 encodes text; builds frame [lenHi, lenLo, payload..., checksum]; computes checksum ONLY over the prefix (two length bytes plus payload) via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; writes checksum as final byte; never computes over the complete frame.
- decodePayload: requires frame length == 2 + L + 1; validates checksum using the same prefix-only java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and compares to (frame[frame.length - 1] & 0xFF); decodes payload as strict UTF-8 and returns String. Throws IllegalArgumentException on length mismatch or checksum mismatch, and CharacterCodingException-derived errors are wrapped or rethrown as IllegalArgumentException.
- bytesToBits: emits exactly eight MSB-first bits per byte using the literal statement bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;.
- bitsToBytes: accepts any non-null bit array length (including 0 and non-multiples of 8). It must literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set each true bit with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));. No modulo-length rejection, exceptions, assertions, early returns, or truncation if bits.length % 8 != 0.

src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: class MatrixValidator { public static void ensureValidSize(int size); public static int capacityBits(int size); }. Semantics: ensureValidSize accepts odd sizes >= 21, else throws IllegalArgumentException. capacityBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask(size) and counts false entries; may round down to multiple of 8; must not double-count or subtract heuristically.

src/main/java/QRDetector.java: class QRDetector { public static boolean[] readDataBits(QRMatrix matrix); public static byte[] extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: readDataBits uses FinderPattern.reservedMask and ZigZag.traversal to read all unreserved cells in order; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes converts all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than two bytes available, throws IllegalArgumentException; reads unsigned length L from first two bytes; computes exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; rejects insufficient bytes; literally truncates via byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); returns frame. It ignores only zero-padded unused suffix dictated by L and never passes all capacity bytes to decodePayload.

src/main/java/QRCodec.java: class QRCodec { public QRMatrix encode(String text); public QRMatrix encode(String text, int size); public String decode(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: encode(String,int) validates size via MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; computes reserved mask and traversal; encodes frame via TextEncoder.encodePayload; writes TextEncoder.bytesToBits into traversal order; leaves all extra unfilled cells false; calls FinderPattern.place; returns populated matrix. encode(String) auto-sizes literally starting with int size = 21; increments by 2 until MatrixValidator.capacityBits(size) >= frameBitLength; delegates to encode(String,int). decode verifies finders via FinderPattern.verify, extracts frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes, and returns TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).

src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: class QRRenderer { public static String render(QRMatrix matrix); }. Semantics: returns a deterministic textual representation with exactly one line per matrix row; no IO side-effects.

src/main/java/Main.java: class Main { public static void main(String[] args); }. Semantics: Demonstrates encode->render->decode pipeline on a fixed short string like "hello-世界"; prints at most one concise line; returns normally.

{"Implementation approach":"Bob (Architect) will deliver a deterministic QR-like codec in Java 11 using Maven with exactly the mandated files. The runtime entry Main is thin and side-effect-free beyond a small fixed demonstration. All core logic is pure and testable, with no GUI or runtime dependencies. The single JUnit 5 test file validates padding, framing, traversal, finder verification, capacity rules, and corruption rejection. We strictly comply with the FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE QR JAVA PADDING CHECKLIST: prefix-only checksum using java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1); TextEncoder.bytesToBits uses the literal MSB-first emission line bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;; TextEncoder.bitsToBytes accepts any bit length and literally allocates byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and sets bits with result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));; ZigZag.traversal performs a two-pass bounded serpentine with exact int[][] result = new int[count][2]; and no while loops; QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes reads all unreserved bits, converts all with the padding implementation, obtains L from first two bytes, computes int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;, truncates with byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);, validates via TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame), and returns frame. FinderPattern.reservedMask/place/verify use a single consistent three-finder definition; QRCodec auto-size literally begins with int size = 21; and increments by 2 until capacity fits. Rendering emits exactly one line per matrix row.

Per-file tasks and contracts ordered by dependency:
1) pom.xml: Java 11 toolchain; depend on org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter in test scope; configure Maven Surefire to run JUnit 5; no runtime deps.
2) src/main/java/QRMatrix.java: Immutable size; boolean[][] cells; construction validating square; getters/setters; copy(); matrix-level helpers used by renderer and validators. No IO.
3) src/main/java/Checksum.java: static int sumMod256(byte[] data): sum bytes as unsigned, return sum % 256. No other functions.
4) src/main/java/ZigZag.java: static int[][] traversal(int size, boolean[][] reserved): two-pass bounded algorithm. First pass counts only unreserved cells and literally allocates int[][] result = new int[count][2];. Second pass iterates rows 0..size-1, columns ascend on even rows and descend on odd rows, appends coordinates only when not reserved. No while loops. No new int[size * size][2].
5) src/main/java/FinderPattern.java: static boolean[][] reservedMask(int size): marks three 7x7 finder squares at top-left, top-right, bottom-left; throws if size < 21 or even. static void place(QRMatrix): sets those finder cells true. static void verify(QRMatrix): ensures those exact cells are true and others in reserved mask remain reserved; throws IllegalArgumentException on mismatch.
6) src/main/java/TextEncoder.java: encodePayload(String text): UTF-8 encode; build frame [lenHi,lenLo,payload,checksum]; checksum computed ONLY over prefix via java.util.Arrays.copyOf(frame, frame.length - 1) and Checksum.sumMod256; never over the complete frame. decodePayload(byte[] frame): verify frame length equals 2+L+1; validate prefix-only checksum with the same Arrays.copyOf; return strict UTF-8 string. bytesToBits(byte[] bytes): exact MSB-first emission with bits[i * 8 + bit] = (bytes[i] & (1 << (7 - bit))) != 0;; bitsToBytes(boolean[] bits): accept any length; literally allocate byte[] result = new byte[(bits.length + 7) / 8]; and set bits via result[i / 8] |= (byte) (1 << (7 - (i % 8)));; no modulo-length rejection or truncation.
7) src/main/java/MatrixValidator.java: static void ensureValidSize(int size): only odd sizes >= 21. static int capacityBits(int size): count unreserved cells (false entries) from FinderPattern.reservedMask(size); may round down to multiple of 8; does not double-count or heuristically subtract.
8) src/main/java/QRDetector.java: readDataBits(QRMatrix): use reservedMask and ZigZag traversal to read every unreserved cell; returns possibly non-byte-aligned boolean[]. extractPayloadBytes(QRMatrix): convert all bits via TextEncoder.bitsToBytes; if fewer than 2 bytes, throw; compute length from first two bytes as unsigned; compute exactly int frameLength = 2 + length + 1;; reject insufficient bytes; literally byte[] frame = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(bytes, frameLength);; validate by TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame); return frame.
9) src/main/java/QRCodec.java: encode(String text, int size): MatrixValidator.ensureValidSize; compute reserved mask; capacityBits; TextEncoder.encodePayload; write bytesToBits into traversal order, leaving any extra cells false; FinderPattern.place; return matrix. encode(String text): auto-size literally starting with int size = 21; while capacity < frameBitsLen, size += 2; then encode(String,int). decode(QRMatrix): FinderPattern.verify; get frame via QRDetector.extractPayloadBytes; return TextEncoder.decodePayload(frame).
10) src/main/java/QRRenderer.java: render(QRMatrix): deterministic string, exactly one line per row, no IO side-effects; e.g., '#' for true and '.' for false.
11) src/main/java/Main.java: small demo: String msg = "hello-世界"; encode; render; decode; print concise result; return normally.
12) src/test/java/MainTest.java: single JUnit 5 file with exactly three tests: (1) Main.main returns normally; (2) bitsToBytes 9-bit fixture yields unsigned 128,128; direct TextEncoder.decodePayload(TextEncoder.encodePayload("hello-世界")) round-trips; QRCodec.decode(QRCodec.encode("hello-世界")) round-trips; rendering has one line per matrix row; (3) corrupting a copied finder cell [0][0] causes decode to throw IllegalArgumentException.
